title: Authentication in Microsoft Entra ID

header.html: Describe the authentication methods; Describe multifactor authentication (MFA); Describe password protection and management capabilities
the official SC-900 study guide, skills measured as of October 21, 2026

html:
1Authentication methods

Microsoft Entra ID supports several ways to prove who you are. They range from weak (password only) to strong (passwordless and phishing-resistant).

Method What it is Strength
Password Something you know Weakest: can be guessed, phished or reused
Microsoft Authenticator app Approve a push notification or enter a code; can be passwordless Strong
Windows Hello for Business PIN or biometric tied to the device; passwordless Strong
FIDO2 security key A physical key (USB or NFC) Strongest: phishing-resistant
Passkey A cryptographic key pair stored on a device or key; phishing-resistant Strong
Certificate-based authentication Sign in with a certificate Strong
OATH tokens Hardware or software code generators Medium
SMS and voice call A code by text or call Weaker: can be intercepted or SIM-swapped
Temporary Access Pass A time-limited code to set up passwordless methods For onboarding and recovery

Passwordless means signing in without typing a password: the user proves possession of a device and (usually) a biometric or PIN. It is more secure (nothing to phish) and easier.

Exam tip

. Strongest and phishing-resistant: FIDO2 keys, passkeys, Windows Hello for Business, certificate-based authentication. Weakest second factors: SMS and voice. Passwordless removes the password entirely.

2Multifactor authentication (MFA)

MFA requires two or more different factor types, so a stolen password alone is not enough.

Factor Examples
Something you know Password, PIN
Something you have Phone with Authenticator, security key
Something you are Fingerprint, face

A password plus a PIN is not MFA (both are knowledge). MFA blocks over 99% of account compromise attacks according to Microsoft. [Verify live]

Ways to require MFA

Way Notes
Security defaults Free, preset protections that require MFA for all users and block legacy sign-in; good for small organizations
Conditional Access policy Flexible rules: require MFA under conditions (module 5); needs P1
Per-user MFA The older way to enable MFA user by user

Exam tip

. MFA = two different factor types. Security defaults = simplest, free. Conditional Access = most flexible ("require MFA when the user is outside the office"). Push fatigue attacks are reduced by number matching in Authenticator.

3Password protection and management

Capability What it does
Microsoft Entra Password Protection Blocks weak and commonly used passwords: a global banned password list maintained by Microsoft plus a custom banned list (for example company names); can be extended on-premises with agents
Smart lockout Locks out attackers after repeated failures but keeps legitimate users working by telling them apart
Self-service password reset (SSPR) Users reset or change their own password after proving identity, which cuts help desk calls
Password writeback Sends a reset password back to on-premises AD in a hybrid setup
Passwordless The best way to avoid password problems

Modern password guidance: length matters more than complexity, do not reuse passwords, check against banned lists and use MFA.

Exam tip

. Banned password list = blocks weak passwords. Smart lockout = stops guessing without locking out real users. SSPR = users fix their own password. Password writeback = needed so SSPR works with on-premises AD.

4Exam Q&A

4.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1Fabrikam Outdoors wants the most phishing-resistant sign-in method for administrators. Which should it choose?

  • AA FIDO2 security key
  • BSMS codes
  • CA longer password
  • DSecurity questions
Show the answer

Answer: A. FIDO2 keys are phishing-resistant and among the strongest methods.

S2A user signs in with a password and then a PIN. Why is this not MFA?

  • ABoth are something you know
  • BA PIN is a biometric
  • CMFA must use SMS
  • DA password is a possession factor
Show the answer

Answer: A. MFA needs two different factor types, and a password and a PIN are both knowledge factors.

S3A small business wants free, preset protections that require MFA for everyone. What should it enable?

  • ASecurity defaults
  • BA custom Conditional Access policy only
  • CMicrosoft Sentinel
  • DAzure Firewall
Show the answer

Answer: A. Security defaults are free preset protections that include MFA for all users.

S4Which feature stops people from choosing passwords such as "Password123"?

  • ASmart lockout after repeated failed sign-ins
  • BMicrosoft Entra Password Protection
  • CSelf-service password reset for forgotten passwords
  • DFederation with an on-premises identity provider
Show the answer

Answer: B. Password Protection blocks weak and commonly used passwords with banned lists.

S5Users forget passwords often and the help desk is overloaded. Which capability helps most?

  • ADefender for Endpoint on company devices
  • BAzure Bastion for remote desktop access
  • CA sensitivity label on every shared file
  • DSelf-service password reset
Show the answer

Answer: D. SSPR lets users reset their own passwords after proving who they are.

S6A sign-in method that uses no password and relies on a device plus a biometric or PIN is called what?

  • AFederation between two identity providers
  • BHashing of passwords before storage
  • CPasswordless authentication
  • DObfuscation of the sign-in page code
Show the answer

Answer: C. Signing in without a password using a device and a biometric or PIN is passwordless.

4.2 Recall questions

R1Which methods are phishing-resistant?

Show the answer

FIDO2 security keys, passkeys, Windows Hello for Business and certificate-based authentication.

R2Which second factors are the weakest?

Show the answer

SMS and voice calls.

R3What does MFA require?

Show the answer

Two or more different factor types.

R4What are security defaults?

Show the answer

Free preset protections that require MFA and block legacy sign-in.

R5What does smart lockout do?

Show the answer

Locks out attackers after failures while keeping legitimate users working.

R6What is SSPR?

Show the answer

Self-service password reset: users reset their own passwords.

5Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Methods password (weakest), Authenticator, Windows Hello, FIDO2, passkeys, certificates, OATH, SMS and voice, Temporary Access Pass
Passwordless no password typed; device plus PIN or biometric; phishing-resistant options
MFA two different factor types; ways: security defaults, Conditional Access, per-user MFA
Passwords Password Protection (banned lists), smart lockout, SSPR, password writeback
